jobs.title: Business Director, Product Strategy & Analysis
jobs.description:
We’re seeking a Business Director, Product Strategy and Analysis, to support strategic priorities for the Consumer and Developer Experience (CDX) leadership team. CDX is an exciting space with diverse product responsibilities. The Consumer and Developer Experience (CDX) organization drives the critical platforms that power world-class digital engagement for our customers and best-in-class tools for the developers who build them. Our diverse portfolio spans the Capital One mobile app, advanced marketing and personalization engines, AI-driven platforms that transform how we build software, and essential enterprise risk and supplier capabilities. By unifying these consumer, developer, and enterprise operations, CDX accelerates our ability to modernize core systems, strengthen the company's risk posture, and deliver seamless experiences at massive scale.

The Business Director will join a horizontal product and strategy team that supports priorities across CDX. The product and strategy team serves as an internal engine for both vision and strategic alignment, occupying a unique space at the intersection of strategic advisory and product creation. We operate with the rigor of top-tier consulting to solve the organization’s hardest strategic questions, drive the annual planning process, and align our long-term priorities. At the same time, we are builders: we act as an innovation lab, developing prototypes and partnering closely with product and engineering teams to translate conceptual visions into tangible, scaled digital experiences. We are looking for a leader who thrives in this duality—someone who is equally energized by big-picture questions about where the world is going, thorny problems that require a strategic mindset and close partnership with product and tech teams, and hands-on building.

Specifically, the Business Director will:

Partner with CDX leaders to define the business strategies for their respective areas
Tackle thorny strategic questions throughout the business, using a consulting-style model
Lead priority strategic initiatives for CDX, such as AI transformation
Support the organization’s intelligence unit, providing analytics, landscape assessments, thematic deep dives, and more to help the organization see around corners and anticipate headwinds and tailwinds
Set the vision for long-term product innovation, including partnering with engineering to deliver product prototypes
Lead a fantastic team of strategy and product people leaders and ICs, investing heavily in their development and creating a pipeline of talent for the organization
Obsess about internal and external customer satisfaction by establishing trusted, close touch relationships with key stakeholders throughout the company
Cultivate a dynamic, customer centric and mission oriented Product culture, fostering collaboration, developing talent
Role model AI adoption by inventing and spreading solutions that improve work efficiency, quality, and fun

The successful candidate will be a great strategic problem solver with a highly collaborative working style. They will excel at building relationships across organizational boundaries and using their strategy toolkit to drive consensus and impact. This leader should have the ability to work through ambiguity with an owner’s mindset and to build product strategy and processes that scale and adapt with growth and market shifts. This leader will be in an exciting position to drive business results, shape organizational culture, and impact both the associate and customer experiences.

Specifically, the Business Director will have:

Exceptional strategy and strategic problem-solving skills, with a record of answering hard questions in ambiguous areas
A strong product orientation, including a record of understanding customers’ needs and working backwards to deliver experiences and solutions that deliver results for the customer and the business
An innovation mindset, characterized by a future orientation, the ability to set a vision, and a willingness to push boundaries
A record of outstanding people leadership, with a style that is collaborative, inspiring, and supportive
Exceptional relationship-building skills that result in trusted partnerships at all organizational levels, across organizational boundaries
Ability to establish credibility with the company’s most senior leaders and with colleagues from different disciplines (e.g., data scientists, P&L owners, designers, engineers)
Intellectual curiosity: an interest in understanding and experimenting with new leading edge technologies, organizational models, and ways of thinking
Demonstrated ability to employ judgment and experience to make rapid and complex decision
Highly effective communication skills (both written and verbal)

Bachelor’s Degree
At least 4 years of experience performing quantitative analysis
At least 4 years of experience performing qualitative analysis
At least 2 years of experience performing people management
At least 2 years of experience performing project management

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Consumer Credit Card
jobs.description:
In 1949, as Diners Club tells it, Frank McNamara finished dinner in Manhattan and found his wallet at home in another suit. His wife came down and paid. He returned to the same table the following February and settled the bill with a piece of cardboard, honored at twenty-seven restaurants and carried by two hundred people, most of them his friends. A year later there were 42,000.

McNamara solved two problems at once. Acceptance: enough restaurants to make the card worth carrying, and enough diners to make it worth accepting. And credit: thirty unsecured days of it, on nothing but a signature. The networks settled acceptance decades ago. What is left is the credit, and the question of why someone carries this card rather than another one. That is this role.

Mercury is building its first consumer credit card. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to define what it is, ship it, and grow it from a first cohort into a portfolio. The scope is the credit account itself: the acquisition and application funnel, the approval experience and the underwriting decisions behind it, how the line moves over time, what the rewards are worth, and the experience of carrying the account day to day.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Key responsibilities:

Build a card people put at the front of the wallet and recommend without being asked
Take the card from zero to launch: decide what ships first, and carry it through program setup and compliance sign-off
Make the approval the clearest and fastest in the category: underwriting owns the model, you own the application, the wait, and the answer
Own how customers experience their line: an increase that feels earned, a decrease that is explained
Own the proposition we take to customers, from rewards and redemption to pricing, and understand the economics that fund it
Set the craft bar: sweat the details, copy, disclosures, latency, empty states, that decide whether a card feels inevitable rather than adequate
Drive the use of AI where it makes the experience meaningfully better: spend that makes sense at a glance, problems surfaced before they are noticed
Make correctness and trust product features: own balances, interest, minimum payments, and statements that reconcile, and be measured on them
Grow the business: own acquisition, activation, retention, and the loops that compound, starting with the businesses Mercury already serves
Align the ecosystem: bring engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, legal, marketing, support, and partners behind one cohesive plan for the card

Some things that might make you successful in a role like this:

A consumer product manager with taste: you have launched products people chose to use, and can point to the decisions that made them work
6+ years building consumer products, including at least one where money moved and errors were expensive
Fluency in credit, or the capacity to acquire it fast: approval rates, line assignment, vintage curves, charge-off, interchange, and rewards liability
An exceptionally high bar for craft, and a customer-centered, data-driven, and experimentation oriented approach
You have shipped AI-led products to real consumers and have opinions about what AI makes possible and where it fails
Exceptional cross-functional collaboration across engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, and partners
Sound judgment in a regulated environment: you balance a delightful experience with the controls a credit product requires, and know which corners are never worth cutting
Nice to have: card issuing, lending, or payments experience, and familiarity with Reg Z and the CARD Act

jobs.title: VP of Product
jobs.description:
About the role:

Curri is seeking a VP of Product to lead and scale the product organization as it enters its next stage of growth. This leader will set a bold, customer-backed vision for an AI-native logistics platform, bring ROI rigor to how we size and prioritize bets, grow the PM team, and be the face of Curri's roadmap in front of customers.

What you will do:

Set and own Curri's product vision and roadmap.
Bake AI into the core of the product so it feels native, not bolted on. No chat sidebars or sparkle buttons. AI should quietly take over the dispatch, routing, pricing, and support decisions people make by hand today, inside the workflows they already use.
Build ROI discipline into the roadmap by putting a value on every opportunity and prioritizing against it, the way Sales manages pipeline value. For automation, that means valuing bets by the ops work they remove.
Close the loop on every bet: define success metrics before building, instrument what ships, and compare actual results against the original estimate. Use that track record to sharpen future sizing.
Work with the executive team to turn company strategy into a focused, prioritized product plan, and represent that plan to leadership.
Partner with Engineering as a true thought partner to work through trade-offs, drive execution, and ship on fast cycles.
Stay close to customers so you understand their workflows and the decisions the platform needs to power. Evangelize the roadmap through customer advisory boards, key account conversations, and joint pitches with Sales that build excitement and help close deals.
Get on sales calls for strategic deals. Run product demos, handle product objections and gaps directly, and help shape what we commit to in enterprise contracts. Bring win/loss patterns back into the roadmap.
Own quality for AI-driven features, including evals, failure modes, cost, and latency, and the guardrails customers need before they trust automation in their operations.
Set the bar for how the PM team works with AI: prototyping with AI tools instead of writing long specs, and moving from idea to working demo in days.
Lead and grow the product management team from three PMs today toward four to six, spending most of your time on leadership and cross-functional work with Engineering, Growth, Operations, and the exec team.

What you need to have:

10+ years in product, including 4+ years managing product managers, with a track record of growing into product leadership where the title reflected real scope.
Strong conviction as a product visionary: you form a clear point of view on where the product should go, ground it in customer evidence, and hold it steady against competing priorities.
Real energy for customer-facing work, from running customer advisory boards to pitching the roadmap alongside Sales, with the ability to leave customers excited about what is coming.
Experience supporting enterprise sales cycles, including demos, product objections, RFPs, and security or integration reviews, with a track record of helping close deals without overcommitting the roadmap.
Business and ROI rigor: experience building business cases for product investments and using opportunity sizing to make and defend prioritization calls.
Strong product analytics instincts. You can define the metrics that matter, pull your own data from tools like PostHog or SQL, and run experiments and staged rollouts without waiting on a BI team.
Shipped AI or ML features to production that users experienced as part of the product rather than a separate add-on, and stayed with them after launch through the messy parts: evals, edge cases, and adoption.
Personal fluency with current AI tools. You use them every day, build prototypes yourself, and have opinions on what is hype and what is leverage.
A hands-on leadership style that pairs executive communication and cross-functional influence with a willingness to roll up your sleeves and do the work alongside the team, rather than managing from a distance.

Bonus points for:

Product leadership experience at a marketplace company.
Having built agentic or automation products in operations-heavy domains like logistics, marketplaces, or field services.
Having built or scaled a product org at a similar growth stage.
Having brought a new layer of discipline, such as ROI modeling or opportunity sizing, to a product team that lacked it.

What is in it for you?

Real space to shape, or overhaul, the roadmap of an AI-native platform, with big bets ahead in automation, internationalization, and expansion into new verticals.
The chance to build and scale the PM team as a true peer to Engineering and Growth leadership.
Competitive salary, equity compensation, and comprehensive benefits (health, dental, vision, 401K).
Remote-friendly with preference for Ventura, CA office presence.
A high-growth, mission-driven environment where your work has direct and measurable impact.

Who are we?

We are Curri, and our mission is to build the network and software that move the world’s goods with speed, intelligence, and trust. Curri provides on-demand, last-mile logistics for construction and adjacent industries with our nationwide fleet of cars, trucks, and flatbeds.

Founded in 2018 and part of the YC S19 Batch, we’re solving the massive inefficiencies that exist in the construction industry. Our headquarters are in Ventura, CA. Learn more at curri.com.

This is a senior product leadership opportunity focused on shaping differentiated solutions for defense and intelligence markets.

You will define product strategy across Earth observation data, geospatial analytics, AI/ML, contextual data, and mission workflows.

The role is highly customer-facing, requiring close engagement with government users, acquisition stakeholders, commercial customers, technical teams, and industry partners.

You will translate complex mission needs into scalable products, clear roadmaps, strong requirements, and compelling commercial offerings.

A major focus will be identifying reusable capabilities, making evidence-based investment decisions, and balancing customer value, market opportunity, revenue potential, and technical feasibility.

You will operate at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Federal, Growth, Sales, Analytics, and Partnerships, driving alignment without creating unnecessary process.

For an experienced product leader with deep U.S. Government defense and intelligence expertise, this role offers substantial influence over strategy, commercialization, and mission-focused technology adoption.

Accountabilities

Define and continuously refine product strategy, roadmaps, investment priorities, and product direction for defense and intelligence offerings.
Lead continuous market and customer discovery with U.S. Government users, mission owners, buyers, program offices, acquisition stakeholders, partners, and industry influencers.
Translate mission problems, customer feedback, and operational workflows into clear product requirements, desired outcomes, priorities, and measurable success criteria.
Identify common customer and mission requirements and turn them into scalable products, reusable capabilities, and configurable workflows.
Distinguish between strategic product investments, reusable customer-driven capabilities, and one-off custom development opportunities.
Make evidence-based recommendations on what to build, improve, package, partner for, or deprioritize based on customer value, market size, differentiation, revenue potential, strategic fit, and technical feasibility.
Convert recurring mission and customer needs into differentiated offerings that can be repeatedly commercialized and delivered.
Partner with Federal, Growth, and Business Development teams to understand funded demand, shape opportunities, support capture activities, and create product proof points that enable revenue growth.
Develop and evolve pricing, packaging, licensing, and value propositions based on customer willingness to pay, acquisition pathways, budget structures, competitive dynamics, and product economics.
Drive the product substance behind customer-facing materials, product briefs, demonstrations, presentations, proposals, use cases, and sales enablement content.
Establish disciplined customer validation processes to assess problems, value propositions, workflow fit, usability, adoption potential, and willingness to pay before and after major investments.
Build a strong operating relationship with Engineering by providing customer context, priorities, requirements, and desired outcomes while allowing technical teams to own architecture and delivery execution.
Work closely with Sales and Market leadership to ensure customer and capture needs inform product decisions without allowing individual opportunities to dictate long-term product strategy.
Monitor competitors and substitutes across commercial Earth observation, GEOINT, analytics, AI/ML, workflow, and data-fusion markets and translate market developments into product strategy.
Communicate product strategy, customer evidence, investment decisions, risks, and performance to senior leadership.
Drive alignment across Product, Engineering, Analytics, Growth, Programs, Partnerships, and Federal leadership.
Define and monitor outcome-oriented product metrics including customer validation, adoption, usage, time-to-value, product reuse, pipeline influence, revenue contribution, and lifecycle performance.
Operate with urgency and responsiveness, proactively identifying customer, market, product, and execution issues before they become escalations.
Maintain accountability through the full product lifecycle, from discovery and requirements through validation, commercialization, and customer adoption.

Requirements

10+ years of product management, product strategy, or closely related product leadership experience, including meaningful experience at Senior Product Manager, Group Product Manager, Principal, Director, or comparable level.
Demonstrated experience taking data-intensive, analytics, geospatial, ISR, AI/ML, or workflow products from discovery through commercialization and adoption.
Strong knowledge of U.S. Government defense and intelligence mission environments, including user and operator workflows and government buying behavior.
Must be a U.S. Citizen.
Must hold a minimum active Secret clearance; active TS/SCI is strongly preferred.
Strong understanding of U.S. Government mission needs, budgets, spending cycles, acquisition pathways, and adoption of commercial GEOINT and Earth observation capabilities.
Experience working directly with customers and users to conduct discovery, validate problems, test concepts, and translate insights into product decisions.
Strong commercial judgment, including experience with pricing, packaging, market segmentation, product positioning, and revenue-oriented product strategy.
Ability to translate complex technical, geospatial, and mission concepts into concise product requirements and executive-level recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to develop customer-facing product materials and represent products in external meetings.
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to lead across matrixed organizations without relying on direct authority.
Ability to balance customer needs, market signals, economics, mission impact, strategic priorities, and technical feasibility when making product decisions.
Comfortable operating in an environment where Product owns market solutions, product strategy, priorities, requirements, and outcomes while Market teams lead capture and revenue execution and Engineering owns technical delivery.
Highly responsive, proactive, evidence-driven, and comfortable making decisions with incomplete information.
Preferred experience with GEOINT, remote sensing, commercial electro-optical imagery, spectral data, SAR, or multi-source geospatial analytics.
Preferred experience working with U.S. intelligence community agencies, COCOMs, Military Services, NRO, NGA, or other civil, defense, or intelligence organizations.

Knowledge of federal acquisition, appropriations, PPBE and budget cycles, OTAs, CSOs, IDIQs, data purchases, software licensing, and other commercial technology adoption pathways is highly desirable.
Experience with product-led capture, market shaping, customer advocacy, or emerging commercial technology adoption is a plus.
Prior military, intelligence community, or federal service experience with direct exposure to analyst, operator, or mission workflows is advantageous.
Washington Metropolitan Area location is preferred.

jobs.description:
In 1949, as Diners Club tells it, Frank McNamara finished dinner in Manhattan and found his wallet at home in another suit. His wife came down and paid. He returned to the same table the following February and settled the bill with a piece of cardboard, honored at twenty-seven restaurants and carried by two hundred people, most of them his friends. A year later there were 42,000.

McNamara solved two problems at once. Acceptance: enough restaurants to make the card worth carrying, and enough diners to make it worth accepting. And credit: thirty unsecured days of it, on nothing but a signature. The networks settled acceptance decades ago. What is left is the credit, and the question of why someone carries this card rather than another one. That is this role.

Mercury is building its first consumer credit card. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to define what it is, ship it, and grow it from a first cohort into a portfolio. The scope is the credit account itself: the acquisition and application funnel, the approval experience and the underwriting decisions behind it, how the line moves over time, what the rewards are worth, and the experience of carrying the account day to day.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Key responsibilities:

Build a card people put at the front of the wallet and recommend without being asked
Take the card from zero to launch: decide what ships first, and carry it through program setup and compliance sign-off
Make the approval the clearest and fastest in the category: underwriting owns the model, you own the application, the wait, and the answer
Own how customers experience their line: an increase that feels earned, a decrease that is explained
Own the proposition we take to customers, from rewards and redemption to pricing, and understand the economics that fund it
Set the craft bar: sweat the details, copy, disclosures, latency, empty states, that decide whether a card feels inevitable rather than adequate
Drive the use of AI where it makes the experience meaningfully better: spend that makes sense at a glance, problems surfaced before they are noticed
Make correctness and trust product features: own balances, interest, minimum payments, and statements that reconcile, and be measured on them
Grow the business: own acquisition, activation, retention, and the loops that compound, starting with the businesses Mercury already serves
Align the ecosystem: bring engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, legal, marketing, support, and partners behind one cohesive plan for the card

Some things that might make you successful in a role like this:

A consumer product manager with taste: you have launched products people chose to use, and can point to the decisions that made them work
6+ years building consumer products, including at least one where money moved and errors were expensive
Fluency in credit, or the capacity to acquire it fast: approval rates, line assignment, vintage curves, charge-off, interchange, and rewards liability
An exceptionally high bar for craft, and a customer-centered, data-driven, and experimentation oriented approach
You have shipped AI-led products to real consumers and have opinions about what AI makes possible and where it fails
Exceptional cross-functional collaboration across engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, and partners
Sound judgment in a regulated environment: you balance a delightful experience with the controls a credit product requires, and know which corners are never worth cutting
Nice to have: card issuing, lending, or payments experience, and familiarity with Reg Z and the CARD Act

jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Bluehost, we believe all small businesses deserve the opportunity to succeed online. Our mission is to give small businesses the confidence to think big. We're the all-in-one platform for small businesses to grow online with powerful simplicity, premium performance, smart tools and human support.

We are entering the agentic era. Our customers — small business owners and the professionals who serve them — will increasingly get work done by delegating to agents rather than clicking through screens. Across the company we are building a growing portfolio of business and product agents: agents that build and optimize websites, agents that market, agents that support and retain, agents that sell, agents that manage the account. Individually they are powerful. Stitched together, they become the product.

That stitching is this role. The Principal PM, Agentic Experiences owns the connective layer — how a fleet of independently-built agents shows up to the customer as one coherent, trustworthy, frictionless experience, across every interface we expose: the customer portal, our APIs, MCP servers, and third-party connectors and channels.

This is a highly cross-functional, high-visibility individual contributor role for someone who thinks in systems, has strong product taste, and can operate in a product-led organization where influence matters more than reporting lines.

What you’ll do & how you’ll make your mark.

The agent experience architecture.
Define the end-to-end model for how agents are discovered, invoked, handed off between, and held accountable to the customer. Own the shared primitives — identity and permissions, context and memory, intent routing, hand-off and escalation, human-in-the-loop approval, transparency and traceability, guardrails and fallback.

Connecting the dots to the customer.
Translate a portfolio of internally-owned agents into a single customer narrative: what the customer can ask for, what happens when they do, how they know it worked, and what it costs. Own the customer journey across agents, not just the agents.

The interface surface strategy.
Set the strategy for how agentic capability is exposed across:

Portal — conversational and ambient agent surfaces inside the logged-in experience, alongside and eventually in place of traditional navigation
APIs — clean, agent-consumable contracts over our commerce, hosting, domains, and account systems
MCP — our capabilities as tools that both our own agents and external agents (Claude, ChatGPT, IDEs, partner platforms) can call safely
Connectors & channels — bringing our agents to where the customer already works, and bringing their tools into ours

Standards and the operating model.
Establish the shared patterns, quality bars, and interaction standards that let a dozen teams ship agents independently without fragmenting the experience. Define what "good" looks like — latency, accuracy, containment, escalation, tone, disclosure — and the review mechanism that holds it.

Measurement.
Define the metric framework for agentic experience: task success and completion rate, hand-off and containment, time-to-value, trust and intervention rates, and the downstream commercial impact on conversion, attach, and retention.

Roadmap and influence.
Build the multi-quarter roadmap for the connective layer, and drive alignment across product, engineering, data, design, care, and marketing to sequence it. Partner especially closely with Data & Personalization — agents are only as good as the context and signals they act on.

Who you are & what you’ll need to succeed.

10+ years in product management, including significant time on platform, API, or ecosystem products, and time on customer-facing experiences. You have shipped both.
Demonstrated ownership of an AI or agentic product surface — assistants, copilots, automation, orchestration, or tool-calling systems in production, with real users and real accountability for outcomes.
Deep technical fluency. You can hold a credible design conversation about LLM orchestration, tool and function calling, MCP, RAG and context strategy, evals, latency and cost trade-offs, and where the failure modes live. You do not need to write the code; you do need to know what you're asking for.
API and platform product judgment. You understand what makes an interface a good contract, and you have opinions about versioning, permissions, and developer experience.
Systems thinker, experience-obsessed. You naturally see the seams between products — and you care, viscerally, when a customer hits one.
Exceptional influence without authority. You can align senior stakeholders across a matrixed, product-led organization, and drive convergence on standards teams actually adopt.
Strong written communication. You write the doc that makes twelve teams agree.
Bias to ship. You'd rather land a real, narrow agentic journey end-to-end this quarter than a perfect framework next year.

Nice to have:
experience in hosting, domains, web presence, SMB SaaS, or e-commerce; experience with agent evaluation and observability tooling; experience building or publishing MCP servers or public developer platforms.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days — a shared, agreed map of every agent in flight across the business; a documented target-state agent experience architecture; one prioritized customer journey selected for end-to-end stitching.
Six months — that journey shipped across at least two interfaces (portal plus API or MCP), with a live measurement framework and adopted interaction standards.
Twelve months — a functioning connective layer other teams build on by default, measurable improvement in task success and time-to-value, and a credible external agent story for partners and third-party platforms.

In 1949, as Diners Club tells it, Frank McNamara finished dinner in Manhattan and found his wallet at home in another suit. His wife came down and paid. A year later there were 42,000.

McNamara solved two problems at once. Acceptance: enough restaurants to make the card worth carrying, and enough diners to make it worth accepting. What is left is the credit, and the question of why someone carries this card rather than another one. That is this role.

Mercury is building its first consumer credit card. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to define what it is, ship it, and grow it from a first cohort into a portfolio. The scope is the credit account itself: the acquisition and application funnel, the approval experience and the underwriting decisions behind it, how the line moves over time, what the rewards are worth, and the experience of carrying the account day to day.

Build a card people put at the front of the wallet and recommend without being asked

Own the proposition we take to customers, from rewards and redemption to pricing, and understand the economics that fund it
Set the craft bar: sweat the details, copy, disclosures, latency, empty states, that decide whether a card feels inevitable rather than adequate
Drive the use of AI where it makes the experience meaningfully better: spend that makes sense at a glance, problems surfaced before they are noticed

Work with the executive team to turn company strategy into a focused, prioritized product plan, and represent that plan to leadership.
Partner with Engineering as a true thought partner to work through trade-offs, drive execution, and ship on fast cycles.

Own quality for AI-driven features, including evals, failure modes, cost, and latency, and the guardrails customers need before they trust automation in their operations.
Set the bar for how the PM team works with AI: prototyping with AI tools instead of writing long specs, and moving from idea to working demo in days.
Lead and grow the product management team from three PMs today toward four to six, spending most of your time on leadership and cross-functional work with Engineering, Growth, Operations, and the exec team.

10+ years in product, including 4+ years managing product managers, with a track record of growing into product leadership where the title reflected real scope.
Strong conviction as a product visionary: you form a clear point of view on where the product should go, ground it in customer evidence, and hold it steady against competing priorities.
Real energy for customer-facing work, from running customer advisory boards to pitching the roadmap alongside Sales, with the ability to leave customers excited about what is coming.
Experience supporting enterprise sales cycles, including demos, product objections, RFPs, and security or integration reviews, with a track record of helping close deals without overcommitting the roadmap.

Support the technical design and development for a complex data system that will center the data around the State resident profile
Scale and communicate the value of a resident-centric data system
Identify areas of artificial intelligence integration to best support the resident experience across a resident-centric data system.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Bluehost, we believe all small businesses deserve the opportunity to succeed online. Our mission is to give small businesses the confidence to think big. We're the all-in-one platform for small businesses to grow online with powerful simplicity, premium performance, smart tools and human support.

We are entering the agentic era. Our customers — small business owners and the professionals who serve them — will increasingly get work done by delegating to agents rather than clicking through screens. Across the company we are building a growing portfolio of business and product agents: agents that build and optimize websites, agents that market, agents that support and retain, agents that sell, agents that manage the account. Individually they are powerful. Stitched together, they become the product.

That stitching is this role. The Principal PM, Agentic Experiences owns the connective layer — how a fleet of independently-built agents shows up to the customer as one coherent, trustworthy, frictionless experience, across every interface we expose: the customer portal, our APIs, MCP servers, and third-party connectors and channels.

This is a highly cross-functional, high-visibility individual contributor role for someone who thinks in systems, has strong product taste, and can operate in a product-led organization where influence matters more than reporting lines.

What you’ll do & how you’ll make your mark.

The agent experience architecture.
Define the end-to-end model for how agents are discovered, invoked, handed off between, and held accountable to the customer. Own the shared primitives — identity and permissions, context and memory, intent routing, hand-off and escalation, human-in-the-loop approval, transparency and traceability, guardrails and fallback.

Connecting the dots to the customer.
Translate a portfolio of internally-owned agents into a single customer narrative: what the customer can ask for, what happens when they do, how they know it worked, and what it costs. Own the customer journey across agents, not just the agents.

The interface surface strategy.
Set the strategy for how agentic capability is exposed across:

Portal — conversational and ambient agent surfaces inside the logged-in experience, alongside and eventually in place of traditional navigation
APIs — clean, agent-consumable contracts over our commerce, hosting, domains, and account systems
MCP — our capabilities as tools that both our own agents and external agents (Claude, ChatGPT, IDEs, partner platforms) can call safely
Connectors & channels — bringing our agents to where the customer already works, and bringing their tools into ours

Standards and the operating model.
Establish the shared patterns, quality bars, and interaction standards that let a dozen teams ship agents independently without fragmenting the experience. Define what "good" looks like — latency, accuracy, containment, escalation, tone, disclosure — and the review mechanism that holds it.

Measurement.
Define the metric framework for agentic experience: task success and completion rate, hand-off and containment, time-to-value, trust and intervention rates, and the downstream commercial impact on conversion, attach, and retention.

Roadmap and influence.
Build the multi-quarter roadmap for the connective layer, and drive alignment across product, engineering, data, design, care, and marketing to sequence it. Partner especially closely with Data & Personalization — agents are only as good as the context and signals they act on.

Who you are & what you’ll need to succeed.

10+ years in product management, including significant time on platform, API, or ecosystem products, and time on customer-facing experiences. You have shipped both.
Demonstrated ownership of an AI or agentic product surface — assistants, copilots, automation, orchestration, or tool-calling systems in production, with real users and real accountability for outcomes.
Deep technical fluency. You can hold a credible design conversation about LLM orchestration, tool and function calling, MCP, RAG and context strategy, evals, latency and cost trade-offs, and where the failure modes live. You do not need to write the code; you do need to know what you're asking for.
API and platform product judgment. You understand what makes an interface a good contract, and you have opinions about versioning, permissions, and developer experience.
Systems thinker, experience-obsessed. You naturally see the seams between products — and you care, viscerally, when a customer hits one.
Exceptional influence without authority. You can align senior stakeholders across a matrixed, product-led organization, and drive convergence on standards teams actually adopt.
Strong written communication. You write the doc that makes twelve teams agree.
Bias to ship. You'd rather land a real, narrow agentic journey end-to-end this quarter than a perfect framework next year.

Nice to have:
experience in hosting, domains, web presence, SMB SaaS, or e-commerce; experience with agent evaluation and observability tooling; experience building or publishing MCP servers or public developer platforms.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days — a shared, agreed map of every agent in flight across the business; a documented target-state agent experience architecture; one prioritized customer journey selected for end-to-end stitching.
Six months — that journey shipped across at least two interfaces (portal plus API or MCP), with a live measurement framework and adopted interaction standards.
Twelve months — a functioning connective layer other teams build on by default, measurable improvement in task success and time-to-value, and a credible external agent story for partners and third-party platforms.
